nodes.label: A police officer's traffic directions take priority even when they differ from ordinary signs, markings or signal indications.

nodes.label: Aggressive-driving behaviors include red-light violations, abrupt lane changes, tailgating, failing to yield and speeding.

nodes.label: Congestion, rushing, construction delays, outside stress and hostile attitudes can contribute to aggressive driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Planning ahead, choosing an alternate route and accepting a late arrival can help prevent aggressive driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: To keep from becoming an aggressive motorist, obey the posted speed limit and remain courteous and patient behind the wheel.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If another driver acts aggressively, let that driver pass and avoid a challenge or eye contact.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook encourages reporting aggressive driving to police and modeling safe behavior for young passengers.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reckless driving involves willful disregard for the safety of people or property.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Negligent driving is careless or imprudent vehicle operation that endangers a person or property.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Vehicle races and speed exhibitions, including drag racing, are prohibited on public roads.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After a crash, stop and remain close to the scene until injured people have been aided and identification exchanged.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Move a crashed vehicle out of the traffic stream when that can be done safely.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Assist an injured crash victim; calling an ambulance is often the appropriate assistance, and a seriously injured or unconscious person ordinarily should not be moved.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Drivers in a crash must exchange their names, addresses and vehicle-registration information and show a license when requested.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If nobody can receive crash information and no officer is present, report the information promptly to the nearest police department.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Crash information also includes the insurer's name and address, local agent or office details and policy-identification number.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When damaging unattended property, try to find its owner; if that fails, leave identifying information securely in a conspicuous location.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Report a crash involving your vehicle to your insurance company.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A motorist who injures a domestic animal should immediately notify the police agency responsible for that location.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before driving, inspect tires, loose items and leaks, adjust the seat and mirrors, buckle up and check the vehicle's signals and brake lamps.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before leaving, consider how light, weather, road conditions and traffic will affect the trip.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Plan a turn early and choose the appropriate lane well before reaching the turning point.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before changing lanes for a turn, check behind and beside the vehicle and communicate the maneuver with the required signal.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reduce speed gradually for an ordinary turn; highway exits instead use the deceleration-lane procedure described in the manual.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before backing, turn to look through the rear window and check both side mirrors rather than relying solely on the inside mirror.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Back slowly and for the shortest practical distance, watching especially for children.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not back into or out of an intersection; use a side street or drive around the block to turn around instead.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When using a driveway to reverse direction, backing into it and leaving forward is safer than backing out.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Use the horn only to warn of an emergency involving a pedestrian, cyclist or another vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A Quiet Zone permits horn use only for an emergency; the horn does not replace braking.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When leaving a driveway or garage, look for nearby traffic and pedestrians, stop before the street and check again.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When backing from a driveway, inspect the space behind the vehicle first and keep checking through mirrors and direct observation.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Supplement turn indicators with hand signals when bright sunlight or vehicles behind obscure the indicators.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Passengers and parcels must not crowd the driver or block the view in any direction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep pets away from yourself while driving, never let them sit on your lap or lean at the driver-side window, and never leave a pet unattended inside the car.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Secure loose cargo away from the dashboard and rear shelf because it can strike occupants during a crash.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep objects away from the accelerator and brake pedals so they cannot interfere with pedal movement.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Beside parked vehicles, anticipate doors opening, bicycles and pedestrians emerging between cars.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reduce speed for intersections, rail crossings, hill crests and curves when conditions require it.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Playgrounds, schools, children, narrow or winding roads and pedestrian hazards require lower speeds.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Weather, road hazards or the driver's condition can require slowing below the normal travel speed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Avoid an unnecessarily low speed that blocks ordinary traffic movement.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Wet pavement reduces traction on curves and lengthens the distance needed to stop.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The beginning of rain can be particularly slippery because water mixes with vehicle fluids that have not yet washed away.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Wet fallen leaves can also make pavement slippery.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water instead of maintaining effective contact with the pavement.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If hydroplaning begins, release the accelerator, hold the steering wheel toward the intended path and let speed fall until control returns.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Flash flooding can develop rapidly after heavy rainfall, even within minutes or hours.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not enter a flooded road; turn around for another route, or wait on higher ground if there is no route available.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Water only six inches deep at a vehicle's underside can cause control loss or a stall.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Two feet of moving water can sweep away most vehicles, including pickups and sport-utility vehicles.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Floodwater can conceal dips or pavement undermined by washed-away ground.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The following-distance example measures the interval after the leading vehicle passes a fixed landmark and treats arriving before a four-second count finishes as too close.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Allow extra following space behind vehicles that make frequent stops, such as buses and mail-delivery vehicles.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The source recommends four or five seconds of following distance in poor weather.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Avoid cutting in front of a truck because it needs additional stopping time and distance.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Stopping distance varies with recognition and reaction, road surface, grade, tire condition, brakes, vehicle condition and wind.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Mental attention to work or family problems increases the workload competing with driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Fatigue, weather and traffic conditions can compound the effects of distraction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Grooming, eating, reading, handling cargo and concentrating on children or pets can all distract a driver.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before using an unfamiliar vehicle, adjust the seat and mirrors and locate its lights, indicators and wipers.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Drowsiness is an early step toward sleep; monotonous long-distance driving can also reduce awareness of the road.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: At the first signs of sleepiness, leave the highway at an appropriate rest or service area to rest or change drivers if possible.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not rely on stimulant stay-awake products to compensate for fatigue.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Unfocused eyes, repeated yawning and difficulty holding the head up are warnings of drowsiness.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Missing an exit, failing to remember recent miles, lane drifting and unstable speed can also signal a sleepy driver.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If tiredness develops, stopping to rest or handing driving to a rested driver is preferable to continuing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep attention on traffic behind, beside and ahead instead of grooming, reading or adjusting entertainment while moving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When upset or angry, calm down before driving or let somebody else drive.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The source requires hands-free cellular use and prohibits texting while driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Secure occupants and cargo and set climate, entertainment and route controls before moving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep tempting reading material out of reach and postpone complex or emotional conversations until arrival.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If a passenger creates a distraction, pull over where legal and safe and resume only when the situation is controlled.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Take a break to eat or drink instead of doing so while driving.
